I am 71 years old, and this plot is all I have — just my one field of maize, about one acre. I learned farming from my mother and father, and I do what my neighbors do. Last season I put one small bag of fertilizer that I got from the government program, and the maize grew better than without it. I do not have money to buy more, but if the program gives me one bag again, I will spread it on my field. I keep my own seed from last year’s harvest — I know it, it fills my stomach, and I do not need to pay for it. I will work the field myself with help from my daughter’s children when they are not in school. I cannot pay anyone to work for me.
